# N64 timing spec

This is the timing model's specification (map [#1](https://github.com/wScottSh/ares/issues/1)). Each row is one behavior: its value, the basis of that value, the reference it comes from, the checks that decide it, and their results. There is no unverified status. A behavior is built from its reference (or, as a model choice, from the reason its reference states), or it is not built. The Code column says where it is built: the constant the code reads, or the code that implements a rule. A row whose value the code does not use is not built, and its Code column says what the code does instead. A check written `pending (gate)` names a corpus the program cannot run yet, and it never counts as verified. A fit row names the checks its value was solved from (fit from). A pass on those verifies the arithmetic, not the model, so a fit row whose other checks only report is labeled **fit only, no independent check**, and its note says why. A check marked (guard) runs and can fail its row, but it never passes it, because it does not measure the row's value: det and stepcap show a run repeats, not that a value is right.

Results come from `behaviors.py --results` over one standing run of every suite, recorded in `docs/spec/n64-timing-results.tsv`. A check is pass, fail, or pending on a named gate. A check that reports its number but asserts none is pending on report-only. Two results are weaker than pass and never count as one. A bench check is consistent-only when a point passes its consistent rule (the hardware band overlaps the model's phase range) but the model's mean over the boot delays misses the band: consistent with the hardware number, not agreement. A bench check is also consistent-only when its verdict is not the same at every code-layout pad (8 pads, one 32 B I-cache line); its detail names each pad's verdict. Every bench range is joint over the pads and boot delays. A hardware check follows the same layout rule: each pad's console capture is compared with the fork's run at that pad, and a question whose fork values differ by pad fails until the console has run every pad. A bench check's detail gives each consistent point's acceptance window (half the band plus half the model's phase range, as a % of the hardware number) and the mean rule's verdict. A check is pass-conditional:#<issue> when it passes only through a model choice with no hardware reference, tracked in that issue. A Thar0 check passes when the model's count lies inside the console's minimum..maximum over its runs. A row's status is fail when any of its checks fails, pass when a check other than its fit data and its guards passes and none passes only weakly (then it takes that weak result), fit only when only its fit data passes, model-choice when a model-choice row has only guards, and otherwise the gates of its pending checks.

| Basis | Meaning | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| measured | a hardware measurement: a test ROM result or a console capture | 33 |
| vendor | Nintendo, NEC or SGI documentation, or a patent | 15 |
| datasheet | a component datasheet | 8 |
| wiki | a community reference: n64brew, or a test suite author's notes | 18 |
| rtl | a hardware description (MiSTer RTL) | 1 |
| derived | computed from other cited values | 9 |
| inferred | reasoned from cited values with no measurement or published value of its own; the note states the inference | 2 |
| fit | fitted to measured data; rounded to the nearest 750 MHz unit | 28 |
| model-choice | no published value; the reference states why the model chose this one | 23 |
| legacy | a constant today's core charges; the reference is its code site and the note names the unit that replaces it | 16 |

| Status | Meaning | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| consistent-only | no check failed, but a check passed its consistent rule while the model's phase mean missed the band, or a bench or hardware check's verdict differs between code-layout pads: some phase or layout of the model agrees with the hardware number, not every one does. Consistent with the hardware, not agreement | 2 |
| fail | at least one check failed; the detail in Check results gives the residual | 25 |
| fit only | only the checks the value was fitted to passed (verify-is-fit) | 12 |
| model-choice | a model-choice row whose only checks are guards: they passed, which shows the choice is built and runs the same every time, not that its value is right | 4 |
| pass | a check other than the row's fit data passed, and none failed | 69 |
| pending:calibration-16 | no check decided the row: calibration-16: no check the program can run decides it: no hardware value is published, or the published one (a vendor figure, a test author's note, or a total over several rows that only guards each of them) has no corpus that measures this row. The console calibration run (#16, hardware only, open) closes it | 13 |
| pending:calibration-16 pending:report-only | no check decided the row: calibration-16: no check the program can run decides it: no hardware value is published, or the published one (a vendor figure, a test author's note, or a total over several rows that only guards each of them) has no corpus that measures this row. The console calibration run (#16, hardware only, open) closes it; report-only: the check runs and reports its number but asserts none; its source names the published value it reports against, or says none is published. Asserting that value, or the console calibration run (#16) where none is published, closes it | 14 |
| pending:no-corpus | no check decided the row: no-corpus: no corpus in the program measures this behavior; it stays pending until one does | 13 |
| pending:report-only | no check decided the row: report-only: the check runs and reports its number but asserts none; its source names the published value it reports against, or says none is published. Asserting that value, or the console calibration run (#16) where none is published, closes it | 1 |

The fit assumes n64brew's memset table was measured with the VI on: the page states no video state (verify-63), and the support is circumstantial, a 128 B write at 17 wire + 1 gap = 18 rclk is 7.11 B/rclk, times (1 - 0.074 VI - 0.0125 refresh) = 6.50, the table's RSP DMA rate. | `sysad.register-write` | 100 units | fit | fit to the n64-systembench era build (50f5066, GCC 12.2): 100 units (8.33 rclk) is where the pass windows of PI I/O W (76..128), SI I/O W (100 and up), SI DMA W ROM (60..108), SI DMA W RAM (108 and below) and PI DMA 128 overlap under main.c's rule (green-plan pisi.md, W sweep and Consequence 2); no hardware measurement of the drain itself (vr4300-wb.md, RCP register row); MiSTer memorymux.vhd:346-425 holds a register write 3 RCP clocks after the 2-SClock address and data phases; n64brew SysAD Interface (non-cached word write, step 4) holds EoK high until the write completes internally, with no cycle count | `pidma:logs` `bench:mi-memset-repeat` `systembench:pi-io-w` `systembench:si-io-w` `systembench:si-dma-w-rom` `systembench:si-dma-w-ram` `systembench:pi-dma-128` `hw:register-write` `hw:wb-drain-target` (fit from `systembench:pi-io-w` `systembench:si-io-w` `systembench:si-dma-w-rom` `systembench:si-dma-w-ram` `systembench:pi-dma-128`) | **fail**: `pidma:logs` fail; `bench:mi-memset-repeat` fail; `systembench:pi-io-w` pass; `systembench:si-io-w` pass; `systembench:si-dma-w-rom` pass; `systembench:si-dma-w-ram` pass; `systembench:pi-dma-128` pass; `hw:register-write` pending:calibration-16; `hw:wb-drain-target` pending:calibration-16 | reads `Timing::Behavior::SysadRegisterWrite` | a posted write to an RCP register, the PI or the PIF takes effect this long after it starts draining. The first PI_STATUS or SI_STATUS read waits behind it, so it anchors the poll grid of every systembench poll row: a busy time moves those readings only in whole poll steps of about 15.3 rclk, and the drain is the continuous lever (pisi.md, Consequence 1 and 2). The five systembench rows chose the value, so their passes check the fit's arithmetic, not the model. The independent check is pidma:logs (rasky's golden logs, a different ROM): PI_DRAM_ADDR, PI_CART_ADDR and PI_WR_LEN are all still posted when t0 is read, so its DMA starts three drains after t0; it places the drain at about 84..108 units on the points that run 4 times at every value (pisi.md). An MI repeat-mode write to RDRAM drains this way too (sysad.cpp throughRi is false while MI repeat is on), so bench:mi-memset-repeat, n64brew's MI repeat memset, checks it; hw:memset-vi decides the table's video state. hw:register-write and hw:wb-drain-target decide the drain on a console |

Its timed instructions are the same in every build measured (GCC 12.1, 12.2 and 16.2), and its reading moves by at most 2 rclk across those builds and every boot delay (sysbench-era), so the check compares the model with hardware at the poll phase that code fixes, under main.c's rule. One to three nops added to each poll step move the reading by up to 10 rclk (verify-83), so the check holds for that instruction sequence only. It replaced bench:pi-io-write, whose poll walk could only show agreement within about ±8 rclk (verify-76). The reading is the store-to-drain time plus a point on the poll grid, which the drain anchors, so a busy time moves it only in whole poll steps of about 15.3 rclk. At the fitted sysad.register-write every busy from 122..139 rclk reads 134 (green-plan pisi.md item 1, measured). systembench:pi-io-w therefore pins this busy only to that window and is fit data of sysad.register-write, so it guards this row and never passes it (green-plan section 8); hw:systembench decides the busy on a console. |

The accumulator starts at V_START with Y_OFFSET and each fetched line adds the Y_SCALE read at its HSYNC once per screen row since the last fetched line (inferred from 'added every scanline'; rows no line fetched take the next fetched line's scale), so with no mid-field write y is the per-line formula's. A mid-frame ORIGIN keeps the accumulated line, as VI_ORIGIN says. ## Legacy costs in today's core

Each row is a constant that today's core still charges. `tools/n64-timing/literal-allowlist.tsv` pins the literal at its code site to the row, so the code and this table cannot disagree. The plan unit in the note replaces the cost and deletes the row.

| `thar0:zcmp` | thar0 | ac-zcmp-zbsame-vioff-noimrd-1cyc | - | suite | Thar0 hw_data. Residual decomposed, not settled (docs/research/thar0-zcmp-residual.md): a one-image read-only line is 10 serial 64 B reads, and the model charges each 45.16 rclk (measured: wire 10.67 + rdp.mem-overhead-read 21 + rdp.span-read-latency 12.5 + 0.98 for the post-to-grant hop, ri.request-latency rounded up to the next rclk edge, exposed because a read posts only when the previous one of its image lands). Hardware's 44.17 rclk per read is Thar0 BUF avg 106000.106 / 240 lines / 10 reads, a whole-run average that also contains any per-rectangle term; the model's per-read cost exceeds it by about the post-to-grant rounding (0.98 rclk). rdp.mem-overhead-read (21) and rdp.span-read-latency (12.5) were grid-fit over the 60 VI-off Thar0 configs, these among them, so an equal cut in rdp.mem-overhead-read fits as well: Thar0 cannot separate the hop, the fit constants and a per-rectangle term; hw:span-width and hw:imrd-zcmp-slots decide it. A build without the hop for DpColor/DpDepth (measured) moves this config -9.68 rclk/line to +0.35%, and every 1-cycle one-image read-only config the same way. Stays failing: removing the hop moves the fit rows' other configs, and the rest (+0.19 rclk/line steady, about 327 rclk once per rectangle) is unexplained |

| `pidma:logs` | pidma | n64_pi_dma_test/pi_dma_test.z64 | - | self | prebuilt rasky n64_pi_dma_test ROM and its 64 golden logs (no license; run from outside the repo, sha256 pinned in standing.sh). ARES_PILOG logs the ROM's own COP0 COUNT reads, and pidma-replay.py pairs each timed DMA start with the reads around it, so the replay is the ROM's own measurement; it is valid only when it reproduces every value the ROM printed (master 78b4427b8: 8 of 8, 23765/24000 within 3% at sizes 8-382). Passes when every point at sizes 8-382, except 305-352, is within the golden min..max +-3%, and the ROM's own 10% self-check reports 0 failures (green-plan.md section 3); no point count stands in for this rule. Sizes 305-352 are excluded and reported only: the golden logs come from the ROM's MODE_GENERATE build, whose cart buffer sits at another PI page phase, so this ROM's DMAs cross a 512 B page from 305 B on while hardware's jump falls at about 353 B (green-plan/pisi.md item 3, inferred) |

The opaque-to-decal cases fail on a model that draws the old mode under the tail (#86). Cycles map 1:1 to tail pixels as in rdpstat:unsynced-combiner; that mapping is the model's reading (n64brew counts the dead cycle at a line end as a pixel for corruption counting, so a 27-cycle window may show 26 visible px), and hw:attribute-stage decides it on the console, so this check is not a console verification |
